title: Nicaea (325)
hook: bishops gather over Arius' teaching and write: of one substance with the Father

segments.voice: Yesterday, Constantine, and your line was freedom for all. Whose different faith did you make room for? Day seven hundred sixty-eight.

One word, and it's Greek: homoousios. It's a mouthful, and yet bishops traveled across the empire to argue over it, emperors took sides, and people were sent into exile for saying it or for refusing to. Here's why. In Alexandria, a priest named Arius was teaching that the Son of God was the first and greatest thing God made. Glorious, above everything else, but made. Not God in the same way the Father is God. His bishop objected. The argument spread, the way arguments do, and the emperor Constantine called bishops together at a city called Nicaea to settle it. Today: the word they chose.

Arius wasn't a careless thinker. He was protecting something: God is one, and nothing can share God's being. So the Son, he reasoned, must be something God made. The creed that came out of Nicaea ended by rejecting a saying of his side, that there was a time when the Son was not. The bishops searched the Bible for words to answer him, Athanasius later wrote, and kept finding that Arius could agree with them. The Son is from God? Yes, he'd say, so is everything. So they reached for a word that isn't in the Bible at all. Homoousios. Of the same being. Of one substance. The Son isn't like the Father in a high and noble way. He is what the Father is. That's the move: a word from outside scripture, chosen to protect what they believed scripture was already saying. John's Gospel opens, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." And Jesus says in John, "I and my Father are one." The bishops heard those lines as more than closeness. The creed later prayed in churches is a fuller form, which we'll meet later on this path. In the old English of the Book of Common Prayer, its lines on the Son run: "Very God of very God, Begotten, not made, Being of one substance with the Father." Very, in that old English, means true. True God from true God. Begotten, not made: a son, not a product. Why does any of this matter on an ordinary day? Because Christians who say this creed are saying that when they look at Jesus, they aren't looking at God's best creation. They're looking at God.
screen: `ARIUS: THERE WAS WHEN HE WAS NOT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: settle, and breathe. If the Nicene Creed is part of your tradition, you can say it now, slowly, from memory or from a page, and stop on the lines about the Son. If it isn't, take just four phrases and let them go by, one per breath. God of God. Light of light. Very God of very God. Begotten, not made. Don't try to solve them. Just notice which one catches. People argued over these words for a long time; you only have to hear them once, slowly. Then let the words go and keep breathing. The bell holds the time.
Homoousios. Greek for of the same being, of one substance. The word the bishops at Nicaea chose to say the Son is what the Father is, not something the Father made.
Your line: true god from true god. Today, notice one word you use without thinking that's actually doing a lot of work, and ask what it's protecting. Day seven hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Christians in Orthodox, Catholic, Anglican, Lutheran and other churches say the Nicene Creed together in worship, standing, often on Sundays.

fork.setup: you're a bishop at Nicaea. every Bible phrase you offer, Arius can agree with. what do you do?
options: keep quoting the Bible until he gives in.
pick one word from outside the Bible that he can't accept.

original.note: Greek: of the same being, of one substance. the word at the heart of the creed of Nicaea.

trapdoor: what you thought: a long, fussy word bishops argued about.
what it means: of one substance: the Son is what the Father is, not something the Father made.
what a scholar hears: a word from outside scripture, chosen because Arius could agree with every biblical phrase offered.

notes: The title carries the date 325 from the index; the spoken script states no date or number of bishops.

The account that the bishops looked for biblical phrases and found Arius' party could accept them, and so chose homoousios, follows Athanasius, De Decretis 19–20. It is his partisan account; confirm framing.
Arius' saying 'there was when he was not' is condemned in the anathemas of the 325 creed; the script paraphrases it as 'there was a time when the Son was not'. Confirm.

The BCP 1662 text is the Niceno-Constantinopolitan form ('the creed later prayed in churches'), not the 325 text. Confirm wording 'Very God of very God, Begotten, not made, Being of one substance with the Father'.
howItsDone names Orthodox, Catholic, Anglican, Lutheran churches as saying the creed; confirm.
